page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARM64 architecture with ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores, this instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz. It features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, delivering 96.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). The processor includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and lacks local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth, reaching 407.39 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 196.56 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Multi-core compute capabilities are reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 23775.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 81853.63, both placing in the upper performance tiers. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1896.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.58.

The server features a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, which supports high-throughput network tasks, as evidenced by a top-tier static web serving throughput of 98.05 GB/sec. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy local database caching or GPU-bound machine learning training. Qualitatively, the ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and compute efficiency for multi-threaded workloads. The c8gb.12xlarge is appropriate for software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, high-throughput web serving, and database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.12xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based server powered by 48 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. It features 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but provides a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, multi-core software compilation, and static web serving throughput, alongside strong multi-threaded decompression and database operations. Conversely, single-core compute and text generation for small LLMs represent moderate to weaker performance areas. This server is designed for multi-threaded workloads, software development pipelines, high-throughput web serving, and containerized microservices.
